What if your AI infrastructure costs dropped 80% overnight? That is not hypothetical anymore.

Model routing techniques are now saving 60% to 90% on inference costs by directing each AI query to the most cost-effective model that can handle it. OpenAI has separately cut its own inference costs by half. And Chinese AI labs like DeepSeek are driving prices even lower with innovations like speculative decoding.

Here is the problem: most enterprises are still running every request through their most powerful — and most expensive — model. That single-model architecture means they are overspending on inference by 5x to 10x compared to what a properly routed system would cost.

The strategic shift is clear. AI projects that were too expensive to scale six months ago may now be economically viable. The bottleneck is no longer whether you can afford to run AI in production. It is whether your architecture is designed to capture these cost reductions.

The companies that restructure their AI stack around these new economics will free up significant budget to invest in AI applications that actually drive revenue — rather than burning capital on undifferentiated compute.
